---
title: "How can I estimate uncertainty in a sample mean?"
---

## Question

How can I estimate uncertainty in a sample mean?

## Decide which method fits

Identify one numeric variable; count usable observations and calculate sample standard deviation; divide that value by the square root of the sample size.

## Worked example: iris

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
result <- ru_apply("standard_error", d, x="Sepal.Length")
stopifnot(result["estimated_se"]>0,result["n"]==150)
```

Standard error describes how a sample mean would vary across suitable repeated samples. It is not the same as standard deviation among flowers. The original Iris observations are not established as a random sample from every species population.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("standard_error", data=your_data, x="numeric_column")
```

If the question asks how dispersed individual observations are, use sample_sd rather than standard_error.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("standard_error")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
